_comment: Curated weeks for the /currents page. Built by tools/build_currents.py from the NECOFS GOM3 hourly hindcast (1978-01-01 to 2017-01-01). 'start' is local midnight; 'hours' is the window length (frames = hours + 1). Add a week here, then rebuild.

weeks.title: Supermoon spring tide
weeks.subtitle: Sep 25 – Oct 2, 2015
weeks.lesson: The Sept 27–28 supermoon eclipse put a full moon at perigee — its closest approach — so these are some of the biggest tides of the year. Watch The Race run over 4 knots, and notice that slack water there comes about two and a half hours after high and low tide at Montauk, not at them.

weeks.title: Summer spring tide
weeks.subtitle: Aug 16 – 23, 2016
weeks.lesson: The Aug 18 full moon lines up sun and moon, so currents peak. Flip between this week and the neap week just before it: same season, same weather — the difference in strength comes from the moon phase alone.

weeks.title: Summer neap tide
weeks.subtitle: Aug 7 – 14, 2016
weeks.lesson: Around the first-quarter moon the sun and moon pull at right angles, so the tidal range shrinks and currents ease. The timing pattern is the same as at springs — slack still lags high and low water — but the water moves far less.

weeks.title: Hurricane Sandy
weeks.subtitle: Oct 26 – Nov 2, 2012
weeks.lesson: Sandy came ashore in New Jersey on the evening of Oct 29, on a full-moon spring tide. Days of strong easterly wind piled water into the Sound — the model puts Montauk about 3 ft above the predicted tide that night. NOAA's predictions know only the moon; the model also feels the wind. Where the dotted model lines pull away from NOAA's solid lines, wind and surge are overriding the tide table — exactly the kind of day a tide app gets wrong.
